Tornado · contiguous US · next 60 minutes

The tornado chance of every tracked storm

For every thunderstorm NOAA’s ProbSevere system is tracking on radar over and near the contiguous United States, the chance that it produces a tornado within the next 60 minutes. This is not a warning: if the National Weather Service issues a tornado warning for your area, take shelter.

Updated
10 Oct 2026, 20:04 UTC
Radar data from
10 Oct 2026, 20:00 UTC
Storms tracked

Map

Quality checks: Published with warnings. The forecast is published; a non-blocking check flagged the following. Full check record

  • Calibration on live forecasts not yet measured (too few closed forecasts with events)

Known input gap. Since NOAA changed the format of its ProbSevere feed on 5 August 2025, the feed no longer carries ProbSevere severe probability and VIL density. The model learned from storms before the change, when they were present; it now receives 0 for them, as it did for the storms after the change in its 2025 test. 3 more inputs the model does not use are missing or in a new format. Every forecast records which inputs were missing. A test written down in advance scored the published model on every storm observation from 2026-01-01 to 2026-09-30 (1,262,285 of them, 1,500 followed by a tornado), all in the new format: AUC 0.9699, against 0.9702 on its 2025 test, so no loss of ranking is visible (2026 is scored on SPC’s preliminary reports). A model built without the inputs the feed lost did not rank better (−0.0003 [−0.0012, +0.0007] AUC, paired by day), so the published model stays. It may cost calibration: over that period the model’s average forecast was 0.81 times the rate at which tornadoes followed. A recalibration for the new format is an open question, to be judged on forecasts made after it is registered (docs/TORNADO_MODEL_PROGRAM.md, amendment 10; results/tornado_program/t2_2026.json).

For tornado warnings, follow the National Weather Service and Storm Prediction Center. HazardPulse publishes research forecasts, not warnings.

About this forecast

What the model is
Gradient-boosted trees on NOAA ProbSevere’s storm attributes — radar, lightning, satellite and the near-storm environment — and the live National Weather Service tornado-warning state
How it tested
On every storm observation of 2025 (1,469,977, of which 1,579 were followed by a tornado), scored once after every choice was fixed: a storm that went on to produce a tornado was ranked above one that did not 97.0% of the time; NOAA’s ProbTor on the same storms, its whole-percent ties broken: 93.9%
What counts as a tornado
a tornado report starts within 10 km of this storm's tracked polygon within 60 min
